meta.scope: Colombia batch 4 — Departmental poverty contrast (Chocó, La Guajira, Sucre vs Cundinamarca/Antioquia), regional hierarchy, and fiscal anchors (DIAN tax collection, royalties, budget). Completes the homogeneity check.
meta.homogeneity_note: Same national GEIH/poverty framework. Capital and Andean departments show much lower monetary poverty; Pacific and Caribbean periphery carry the highest rates.

candidates.title: Departamento del Chocó — highest-poverty contrast
candidates.description: Pacific department with the highest monetary-poverty incidence in the 2025 departmental results. Tests the statistical hierarchy under extreme marginalisation.
candidates.notes: Poverty-contrast department. 2025 monetary poverty 65.3% (highest of the 23 reported departments); extreme poverty also the highest. National survey infrastructure reaches the department; independent local statistical density is thin.

candidates.title: Departamento de La Guajira — high-poverty Caribbean contrast
candidates.description: Northern Caribbean department with the second-highest monetary-poverty incidence. Completes the periphery contrast alongside Chocó.
candidates.notes: 2025 monetary poverty 60.2%. Extreme poverty also elevated. Illustrates the Caribbean–Pacific poverty belt under a common national measurement framework.

candidates.title: Departamento de Sucre — secondary high-poverty node
candidates.description: Caribbean department ranking third in monetary poverty in the 2025 results.
candidates.notes: 2025 monetary poverty 51.8%. Reinforces the Caribbean high-poverty cluster.

candidates.title: Departamento de Cundinamarca — low-poverty contrast
candidates.description: Andean department surrounding Bogotá with the lowest departmental monetary-poverty incidence in 2025.
candidates.notes: 2025 monetary poverty 15.1% — lowest of the reported departments. Completes the capital-region low-poverty pole opposite Chocó/La Guajira.

candidates.title: Departamento de Antioquia — core statistical identity
candidates.description: Major Andean department centred on Medellín. Intermediate-to-low monetary poverty and a relatively dense urban statistical presence via the Medellín AM domain.
candidates.notes: 2025 monetary poverty 19.2%. Hosts the second-largest metro and a significant share of manufacturing and services activity.

candidates.title: Pobreza monetaria por departamento (DANE)
candidates.description: Official departmental tabulations of monetary poverty and extreme poverty. Primary source for the inter-departmental poverty gradient.
candidates.notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 ranking (selected): Chocó 65.3%, La Guajira 60.2%, Sucre 51.8%, … Antioquia 19.2%, Bogotá 17.8%, Cundinamarca 15.1%. National average 28.0%.

candidates.title: DIAN — recaudo tributario y aduanero
candidates.publisher: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
candidates.description: Tax and customs administration. Publishes gross and net tax collection by type of tax (income withholding, VAT, customs, etc.) and performance against annual targets.
candidates.notes: Primary revenue-side fiscal statistic. 2025 gross collection ~COP 296 trillion (96.9% of target). Links the real-side economy to the central-government budget.

candidates.title: Sistema General de Regalías / Royalties from hydrocarbons and mining
candidates.publisher: Ministerio de Hacienda / DNP / Agencia Nacional de Hidrocarburos
candidates.description: Royalties generated by hydrocarbon and mineral extraction and their distribution to producing and non-producing territorial entities. Major sub-national fiscal transfer mechanism.
candidates.notes: Critical sub-national fiscal node. 2025 hydrocarbon royalties caused ~COP 8.5 trillion. Concentrated in Meta, Casanare, Santander, Arauca and Huila. Directly links the oil/mining production statistics to territorial budgets.

candidates.title: Presupuesto General de la Nación / National Budget
candidates.publisher: Ministerio de Hacienda y Crédito Público
candidates.description: Annual national budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues and expenditure of the central government.
candidates.notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links tax collection (DIAN), royalties and other revenues with functional spending on education, health, social protection and investment.

candidates.title: Departamento del Valle del Cauca — core statistical identity
candidates.description: Major Pacific-Andean department centred on Cali. Intermediate monetary poverty and a significant metropolitan domain (Cali AM).
candidates.notes: 2025 monetary poverty 21.8%. Completes the set of large departmental economies alongside Antioquia, Cundinamarca/Bogotá and the Caribbean departments.

proposed_edges.basis: Departmental poverty tables are geographic disaggregations of the national monetary-poverty measurement.
Chocó’s high poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
La Guajira’s high poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
Cundinamarca’s low poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
Royalties are generated by hydrocarbon and mineral production.
Tax collection is the primary revenue source of the national budget.
Medellín Área Metropolitana is the principal urban core of Antioquia.
